messages:
jun: noticed a regression on canary after enabling group-stride kernel handoff for AWQ weight-only int8. p95 for short chats jumped from ~23ms to ~28ms, p99 tails worse. low QPS but repro easily with seq<=64 :thinking:
owen: can you paste the canary run logs? which kernel got chosen at inference time?
sara: fwiw we saw similar tail behavior when pack overhead dominates for tiny batches — packing costs + dequant path can outweigh savings unless group-size aligns with batch.
jun: logs attached below (excerpt). kernel chooser picked `int8_stride_v2` then fell back to `dequant_scalar` on some requests. sequence: 16/32 mostly.
```
[2026-02-18T10:12:34Z] request id=rt-9a2 chosen_kernel=int8_stride_v2 group_stride=12 batch_size=1 seq_len=24 latency_ms=31.8
[2026-02-18T10:12:34Z] request id=rt-9a3 chosen_kernel=dequant_scalar group_stride=12 batch_size=1 seq_len=24 latency_ms=47.1
[2026-02-18T10:12:34Z] request id=rt-9a4 chosen_kernel=int8_stride_v2 group_stride=16 batch_size=4 seq_len=64 latency_ms=19.4
```
li: hmm that second line suggests fallback happened mid-request maybe due to failed kernel precondition (alignment mismatch) or OOM on workspace allocations. did you see any kernel errors?
jev: (perf-bot) automated microbench ran shortly after the deploy and reported: 
```
model: awq-gpt2-medium-int8
configs: group_stride=[8,12,16,24] batch=[1,4,8] seq=[16,32,64]
metrics: p50/p95/p99 ms
group_stride=8 batch=1 seq=16 -> 18.2 / 22.9 / 39.5
group_stride=12 batch=1 seq=16 -> 19.6 / 28.1 / 52.0  <-- tail regression
group_stride=16 batch=1 seq=16 -> 17.9 / 23.4 / 40.2
pack-overhead ~= 0.34ms per req when group_stride != batch-friendly
```
jun: thanks perf-bot. pack-overhead ~=0.34ms matches our instrumentation (bytes copied + rebuffer + group quantize). for small batches that dominates and the chooser didn't prefer the scalar path consistently.
owen: why did chooser pick int8_stride_v2 for group_stride=12 at batch=1? chooser rule currently: prefer quant kernel if estimated_tokens_saved_per_sec > threshold, ignoring per-request tail penalty. that's the bug.
sara: propose heuristic change: for seq<=64 and batch<=2, prefer kernel with lower p95_tail metric (we already have historical tail_estimates per-kernel). fallback to quant only when throughput advantage > X and tail delta < Y.
mike: sounds reasonable. what about KV-cache hotpath? pack/unpack interacts with KV buffer layout and causes memcpy into pinned memory which can add nondeterministic stalls on tail. we should measure hotpath evictions.
li: quick instrument plan: add counters for pack_memcpy_us and kv_buffer_eviction_count and expose via /metrics. also add per-request kernel_selection_reason tag to traces.
eva: rolling back automatic handoff to `int8_stride_v2` for canary while we iterate? we can do a canary flag in runtime to disable handoff, leave manual opt-in.
jun: plan: 1) revert handoff for canary (roll to 0% auto), 2) add metrics & traces, 3) change chooser heuristic to prefer p95 for small sequences, 4) run A/B for 24h. I'll open a PR.
li: for local repro, run this bench:
```
./bench_infer --model awq-gpt2-medium --kernel-candidates=int8_stride_v2,dequant_scalar --group-size=12 --batch=1 --seq=16 --iters=2000 --trace-selection
```
mike: also test mixed batches (1,4) since runtime batching mixes sizes. suggest adding a microbench that randomizes batch mix to capture packing overhead variance.
sara: if chooser rule changes, add unit tests: simulate seq distribution skewed to small sequences and ensure selection matches lower-tail kernel.
perf-bot: posted perf-diff summary for the last deploy: 
```
canary: qps=3.2 -> unchanged
p50: 18.9 -> 19.2 (+1.6%)
p95: 22.7 -> 28.4 (+25%)
p99: 39.8 -> 52.0 (+30%)
```
jun: thanks. filing incident ticket and PR now. will tag owners and schedule A/B.
deploy-bot: rollback action queued for canary if p95 > 30ms for > 5m. :information_source:
owen: thumbs up to that automation. once we have traces we can safely adjust chooser weights. :thumbsup:
